title: Add a persistent SQLite cache
description: Adds `cachetools.sqlite.SQLiteCache`, an LRU cache kept in an SQLite file, so a function decorated with `@cached(SQLiteCache(...))` keeps its results across restarts. Each cache lives in its own table (`table`, default `"cache"`; any string is a valid name), so several caches can share one file. Keys and values are pickled and keys are matched by their pickled form; as with `shelve`, only open files you trust. `maxsize` bounds the number of items: storing a new key in a full cache evicts the least recently used item. Reading an item with `cache[key]` counts as a use, checking `key in cache` does not, and storing a new value for a key that is already in the cache never evicts another item. With `ttl`, an item expires `ttl` seconds after it was stored, by the same rule as `TTLCache`, measured with `timer` (`time.time` by default, because items outlive the process). A value that cannot be pickled raises and leaves the cache as it was. Includes tests.

defects.summary: The table name is wrapped in double quotes without doubling the quotes inside it, so a table name containing a double quote breaks or rewrites every statement.
Items count as live while expires >= now, so an item is still returned exactly ttl seconds after it was stored, unlike TTLCache and unlike expire().
A read sets used to used + 1 instead of past the current maximum, so a read item does not become the most recently used and is evicted before items used later.
`key in cache` goes through __getitem__, which marks the item as used, so membership checks change which item is evicted.
defects.corrected:
row = self.__execute(
            "SELECT 1 FROM {table} WHERE key = ? AND (" + _LIVE + ")",
            (pickle.dumps(key), self.__timer()),
        ).fetchone()
        return row is not None

defects.summary: The value is pickled only after an item has been evicted, so storing a value that cannot be pickled raises but has already evicted an item from a full cache.
defects.corrected:
v = pickle.dumps(value)
        now = self.__timer()
        self.expire(now)
        self.__evict(k)
defects.defective:
now = self.__timer()
        self.expire(now)
        self.__evict(k)
        v = pickle.dumps(value)

defects.summary: Eviction counts the key being stored, so replacing the value of a key already in a full cache evicts another item.

ceiling.summary: The lookup in __getitem__ appends _LIVE after AND without parentheses, and _LIVE is an OR, so the query reads (key = ? AND expires IS NULL) OR expires > ? and a missing key returns whichever item with a ttl has not expired yet.

decoys.why: Only the table name is formatted into the SQL, and it is already a quoted identifier; every value goes in as a parameter.
The parameter shadows the time module only inside expire(), which does not use the module; the signature matches TTLCache.expire.
